extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting to PeerJ and reviewers/editors participating in PeerJ's peer-review process
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for submitting manuscripts to PeerJ and for performing editorial and peer-review duties (scope, acceptable article types, review criteria, editor/reviewer responsibilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of subjects accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ is an Open Access, peer-reviewed, scholarly journal. It considers articles in biology and life sciences, medicine and health, environmental science, chemistry and materials science, engineering and technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PeerJ does not publish in the Social Sciences or Humanities (except where articles in those areas have clear applicability to the core areas of science and engineering). Articles are published on a continuous schedule (new articles Monday–Friday).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted article types
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ considers Research Articles, Bioinformatics Software Tools, Systematic Review/Meta-Analyses, Literature Review Articles, Method Articles, Data Reports and Registered Reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PeerJ does not accept Hypothesis Papers, Commentaries, Opinion Pieces, Case Studies, Case Reports, etc. If unsure whether an article meets requirements for a submission type, authors should consult the discipline standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation principle: scientific and methodological soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ evaluates articles based on an objective determination of scientific and methodological soundness, not on subjective determinations of 'impact,' 'novelty' or 'interest'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The objective is to judge whether an article should join the Scientific Literature; specific guidance for assessing aspects of submissions is given under the Editorial Criteria (Basic Reporting, Experimental Design, Validity of the Findings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on research integrity and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ applies the highest standards to everything it does—specifically, the publication places an emphasis on research integrity; high ethical standards; constructive peer-review; exemplary production quality; and leading-edge online functionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These values inform editorial decisions and expectations of submissions and review conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher right to decline submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ reserves the right to decline to consider, or publish, any submissions for any reason at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can include studies that do not have a grounding in established scientific knowledge, conflict with PeerJ's core values, are outside scope, or fail to satisfy technical or editorial policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review evaluation categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are peer reviewed against criteria grouped into 3 broad categories: Basic Reporting; Experimental Design; Validity of the Findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specific guidelines for each of these categories can be found on the Editorial Criteria page (see that page for detailed checklists/examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic Editor oversight and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions which pass basic submission checks are peer reviewed and the peer review process is overseen by an Academic Editor on the Editorial Board. Academic Editors are experienced scientists in their field and act independently from PeerJ to make independent decisions on submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Academic Editors exercise editorial judgment and are responsible for the outcome for assigned submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic Editor duties: solicit reviewers and decide
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual Academic Editors take on responsibility for individual submissions. They solicit expert peer reviewers to comment on the article and they make an editorial decision based on their knowledge of the field utilizing the input of those reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions should integrate reviewer input with the editor's domain expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum external review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic Editors are not permitted to accept a submission unless it has been reviewed by at least one external reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On average, PeerJ expects that all submissions will be reviewed by two peer reviewers (in addition to the Academic Editor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic Editor confidentiality, COI and ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic Editors are required to treat all submissions confidentially; to declare any potential conflicts of interest; and to adhere to the highest prevailing standards of publication ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These obligations govern handling of manuscripts and decision-making processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of acceptance decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academic Editor who made the Acceptance decision is named on all published articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming the accepting editor provides transparency and accountability for editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct: unbiased, constructive, timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are expected to provide unbiased and constructive feedback in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be helpful to authors and editors and returned within timelines appropriate to the journal's processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer confidentiality and AI-upload prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are required to maintain the confidentiality of the review process. Material under review should not be shared or discussed with third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under no circumstances should any manuscripts or other submission files be uploaded to generative AI tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer disclosure obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must disclose any potential conflicts of interest and the use of AI-assisted technologies when writing their report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures help editors assess potential biases and the provenance of review text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer identity and public review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are encouraged to provide their names. All reviews (anonymized or not) of published articles are made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PeerJ operates a transparent review policy where reviews for published articles are posted; reviewers may choose to sign their reports to be identified.
